lines.text: A virus gets in... and copies itself, fast.
A vaccine shows your body a harmless copy. Same spikes, but it can't multiply.
Only the immune cell whose shape fits locks on.
It multiplies, and makes antibodies that grab the copies.
When it's over, a few cells stay behind... as memory.
If the real virus shows up, memory cells know it at once, and stop it early.
But viruses change, and protection fades. That's what boosters are for.
